regime_context: TSX leadership is concentrated in precious metals — Silver & Royalties is the narrow leader (score 2.078) with Gold Miners the close challenger (1.933, margin 0.145). The absolute-trend gate is validated for this market (gate_helps=true), so staying-power discipline is real, but cross-sectional momentum itself has no forward edge. Track record (n=62, dir_accuracy 0.306) says directional calls have been poor — lean low.
emerging_watch: Watch whether the confirmed precious-metals leadership (Silver & Royalties + Gold Miners) hands off to Base Metals & Copper — the only crowded theme in the top ranks. If Base Metals' crowding_z falls below 1.0 while its rank stays top-3 and precious metals lose trend-gate eligibility, that would mark a confirmed leadership shift worth re-reading.

theses.subject: Silver & Royalties
theses.thesis: Silver & Royalties is the confirmed leader with durability_bar 0.7, breadth 1.0, and not crowded. The only validated edge here is the absolute-trend gate (eligible=true), which supports staying with the trend rather than fading it. I express no view on return magnitude; the lean is that leadership persistence is the better default until the trend gate flips.
evidence: rank 1 with score 2.078, margin over challenger 0.145
crowding_z 0.86, crowded=false — no size-down caution triggered
theses.dissent: Silver and gold miners are highly correlated; this is effectively one precious-metals beta. If silver spot mean-reverts after a sentiment spike, the royalty complex falls hardest, and track-record dir_accuracy of 0.306 warns against trusting the leader for direction.

falsifier.text: Silver & Royalties (XGD.TO proxy) loses its eligible=true trend-gate status before the check-by date

theses.subject: Gold Miners
theses.thesis: Gold Miners ranks second with similar durability (0.75) and full breadth, also not crowded. The rotation margin to the leader is thin (0.145), so treating the two as a single precious-metals leadership complex is defensible while both hold trend-gate eligibility.
theses.dissent: The two precious-metals themes share the same proxy (XGD.TO), so there is no diversification between these leans — they are one bet on precious metals. If gold breaks down on a stronger USD or higher real rates, both fail together.

falsifier.text: Gold Miners falls out of the top-2 eligible set and durability_bar drops below 0.6 before the check-by date

theses.subject: Base Metals & Copper
theses.thesis: Base Metals & Copper ranks third and is eligible, but it is the one crowded theme in the leadership band (crowding_z 1.19, crowded=true). Guardrails say crowding is a size-down caution, not a fade — so this is an avoid/underweight signal for new exposure, not a short.
evidence: crowding_z 1.19, crowded=true — only crowded theme in top ranks
theses.dissent: Copper has idiosyncratic supply/tightness drivers that are not captured by the crowding flag; crowding has no basket-level forward edge and could simply mark genuine fundamental demand.
